content.text: InstagramLog InSign UpCloseNever miss a post from galaxiesSign up for Instagram to stay in the loop.Sign upLog inAudio is mutedgalaxies•FollowMore optionsgalaxies 17wThe last time humans went to the Moon was during NASA’s Apollo 17 mission, which landed on December 11, 1972, with astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt walking on the surface, making them the last people to walk on the Moon to date. Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface, marking the end of the Apollo era of Moon landings.A few moments before stepping off the Moon’s surface for the last time and climbing back into the lunar module, Cernan stopped to mark the occasion of Apollo’s last footsteps through a brief speech with an eye for the future.“…as I take man’s last steps from the surface, back home, for some time to come, but we believe not too long into the future, I’d like to just list what I believe history will record that America’s challenge of today has forged man’s destiny of tomorrow. And, as we leave the Moon at Taurus-Littrow, we leave as we come and, God willing, as we shall return, with peace and hope for all mankind.
